chapter: Wider talk: bands, places and players
title: Recording with Roger Wolfe Kahn on piano and drums
summary: With Roger Wolfe Kahn he made four sides of piano and drums for a Treasury show, using a rag in the snare.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: My first record date: sessions, personnel, discography

blocks.x: Well, he was playing there, just, just doing a single, see? Oh, yeah. And, uh, that's, that's when, when we got together with Roger Wolfe Kahn, uh, Roger Wolfe Kahn. Roger Wolfe.

Roger Wolfe. And, and we made these records, see? Mm-hmm. And, and we did, we, we got the band together and we did that, that, uh, that, uh, Treasury show. We made four sides. We made, uh, Breezing Along and, uh, Little Rock Getaway. Um, I don't know, there was three songs that, that, that, that, uh, uh, what's his name, wrote, see, his own songs, see? It was just piano and drums, see? But, uh, we had, uh, a, a sheet in between us. He, there was a piano over there and, and, and, and, I'm, I'm set up over here. But, uh, my, my, my, my, my, my, my snare drum, see, the buzz while, while, while, while, while, while, while he was playing there or something under him. And that's why I put a, a rag in it. So, the snare drum sounds a little different than, than, than, than an ordinary would, see? So, that, that's why, it, it, it was crisp. A little bit too, couldn't, didn't have the sound, the sound of a snare drum, see? So, I don't know. We tried it out, and, like, I, like, I, I, I played a lot of them. Things in the wood block, the cowbell, the little things, like Baby Dotson do, you know? So, I don't know, but.
Did you tap dance? Huh? Did you tap dance on any records? No, no.
No, you didn't do any dance?
No, I, I, I didn't do any dance.
